narrative:
Nothing has shipped yet, so there is no shipping velocity to report. Across two requests reviewed, both on Nov 2, 2026, each is about 70 percent done and committed, with no PR merge or release recorded. Ask-to-commit time is under ten minutes for the first pieces, but ask-to-ship is still unknown.

## ISO 8601 duration formatting in ms (Nov 2, 2026)

At 18:16 the owner asked for ISO 8601 duration support in the ms library, starting with formatting. They gave two examples: formatISO(5400000) should return "PT1H30M", and 90061000 should return "P1DT1H1M1S". They set days as the largest unit, because months and years are ambiguous. They also asked for the function to be exported from src/index.ts and covered by tests.

formatISO was added with its own test file and committed as e2ceaf8 (obs 2, 3). The owner then said a security reviewer wants no regular expressions in any new parsing code on this branch, so the parse side had to be hand-written. About seven minutes later a new conversation continued with parseISO as the inverse of formatISO. It handles weeks, days and time parts, an optional sign, and comma or dot decimals. It returns NaN for years and months. A trailing-T case such as "P1DT" was fixed to be rejected (obs 16, 17). Round-trip tests were added and the full suite passed at 188 tests (obs 18). Memory shows no commit of parseISO, PR, release or owner confirmation yet. One open question is that later observations mention a /t$/i test, which sits uneasily with the no-regex constraint.

## parseCompound for strings like "1h 30m" (Nov 2, 2026)

At 18:20 the owner asked for a separate PR adding parseCompound, with an export from src/index.ts and tests. feat/compound already held the formatISO commit, so the agent cut feat/parse-compound from main (obs 4, 6). parseCompound was committed as 7ed8d44 (obs 9, 10).

The owner then asked for a single anchored regex for the whole string, in the style of parse(), with a capped input length, because the reviewer prefers that. The work was reworked to an upfront anchored validation regex plus a matchAll loop and a 100-character limit, and committed as 6cc46a1 (obs 11, 12). That is one rework within about a minute. No PR opening, merge or release is recorded.

## What this suggests so far

The owner writes specific asks. They give concrete examples, name the file to export from, ask for tests in the same request, and state design limits up front. They pass on reviewer constraints as they learn them, and these can differ by branch: no regex on the formatISO and parseISO branch, an anchored regex on the parseCompound branch. They also keep separate features in separate PRs. Later chapters should record how long it takes from these asks to a merged and released change.
